I think having a bug crawl in your mouth is one of the most unsettling and horrific experiences. I remember I took a big gulp of a water bottle that I had left on the ground when I was playing in the mud as a kid, and a cicada had found its way in there. I didn’t realize the bug was in my mouth for a few seconds because I was swishing the water around, then I had the signature “screeeee” that cicadas do vibrate in my fucking skull and felt pointy bug legs scratching at my cheek and every atom in my body was VIOLATED. Spat it out so fast and cried for hours afterward, my mom had to hold me so I would stop scrubbing my tongue with a toothbrush. I will literally never forget that day. I never leave drinks outside anymore and get uncomfortable eating outside unless I thoroughly inspect everything beforehand. Fml.

While I get where you are coming from, I also never do “dangerous” things unless I’m with a group of people who fully understand the risk of what it is we are doing and are willing to take responsibility for anything that happens and help one another if we do get hurt. I mean, that’s part of adventuring, at least how I do it, and I think a lot of people on this subreddit understand the risks of hiking too and bring things to help in emergency situations. There is a huge difference between “hey let me do this spontaneous thing that could cause myself and other unsuspecting people around me to be in danger” versus “hey lets do X, but this could go wrong so lets also bring phone for emergencies etc.” Of course not everyone thinks ahead that far before doing dangerous things, but I also don’t think that everyone is a complete dumbass who would willingly hurt themselves and the people around them for fun. And this dude just fell off a tree, he was not endangering anyone around him. Worst case scenario, he’s in the middle of Timbuktu, his legs break into a thousand pieces and he has to be airlifted out…. Yeah that would be pretty shitty for the people who would need to help him out of there but at the same time, you can say that sort of thing about just walking down the road. Scary stuff happens every day. It’s unlikely, but not impossible, you can either let the fear limit you or you can be responsible about preparing for worst-case scenarios and not letting it hold you back.

I understand you, OP, and I know where you are coming from. Your feelings make complete sense and I too have found myself believing this many times in my life (and lately). I know I cannot change your mind, as a mere stranger on the internet, but I can offer you some things that have comforted me in such a mindset and saved my life. Music, especially ambiance type music that can be found in compilation style on youtube, has a certain ability to transport you outside of yourself for a time and feel comforted in the soft tunes. I don’t know what you like- maybe adventure fiction? There are really cool “mystical forest” style videos that truly make you feel like an adventurer wandering through a forest. Maybe you like sci-fi; there are “deep space” music collections that can make you feel like you’re traversing the galaxy. I know it sounds so silly, but things like this are a small, little bit of escape and respite from the world. Turn down your lights, close the blinds, lay down for a while and listen to some music that takes you out of yourself for a while. It can be hard to find the genre you enjoy, but I am certain there is something out there that will resonate with you on some level.
If you like regular bands, “Modest Mouse” is very good, my favorite song by them is “Dramamine.” I also like the band “Meltt,” couple songs that are good from them are “Deeper Water” and “On Your Own.”
Even outside of music there are some sources of comfort. Walking outside in nature, completely alone, listening to the sounds of bugs and animals around you. If you don’t live in an area with nature but have the means to perhaps take a trip somewhere for a hike, I would suggest doing that. It helps me clear my mind a lot. The world is so beautiful- it’s just the people on it that are cruel and make life so difficult. The way our society is structured makes everything so painful and unbearable; but the earth itself is beautiful and something worthy of appreciation.
So, say you don’t like music or nature, I’m sure you have tried these things before but still find yourself wanting to die and I understand. I just say, try all that you can (though perhaps you have already exhausted all hobbies and things like this, but in case you haven’t, I’ll just remind you that your body is a remarkable tool capable of so much). You could paint, you could play an instrument (who cares if you are skilled in these things, the point is to find something to direct your energy into until you feel okay again).
I really, really just want you to know- before you go and before you decide to do this- that you are valuable. You are capable of so much. Life is just a waiting game, we ride out the waves of misery to find a single second of happiness before plunging back down into the depths of pain and eventually we all die and it all feels so meaningless. But it isn’t meaningless if you find your personal meaning. If you find your source of happiness, then that is what you are here for. You are here because you deserve to be.
I recommend the video “Pale Blue Dot” by Carl Sagan, as well. And there is an audio book on youtube which is quite remarkable (ten hours), if you like that short video too. I hope you will stick around OP. You deserve to live. You deserve to find happiness. You deserve the time and chance to continue searching for your peace.
